title: REBUILD Experiment Card
description: One experiment with its comparison, guardrails and decision rule fixed before it runs. Rejects semantically empty cards: a test with no control, no guardrail or an unstated decision rule is not a test.

hypothesis.description: Falsifiable statement, phrased so a result could disprove it.

evidence_grade.description: Grade of the evidence the hypothesis rests on.

audience.description: Who is exposed, and the eligible population.

control.description: The comparison condition. Required for any causal claim; an empty control means there is none.

primary_metric.description: The single decision metric; an outcome or diagnostic measure, never an activity measure such as impressions.

primary_metric_definition.description: Numerator, denominator, window and source of truth.

guardrail_thresholds.description: A guardrail without a threshold cannot stop anything; name the level at which the test halts.

additionalProperties.description: The level at which this guardrail stops the test.

minimum_detectable_effect.description: The effect the design can detect. If this cannot be stated the result may only be reported as directional.

value.description: Minimum detectable effect, absolute or relative, with units.

method.description: How it was derived, e.g. two-proportion z-test at 80% power.

baseline.description: Baseline rate or value the MDE is relative to.

available_n.description: Units actually available. If below n_per_arm the result is directional only.

adequate.description: True only when available_n >= n_per_arm; false forces a directional-only claim.

sample_logic.description: Required sample or exposure, and the reasoning.

duration.description: Planned window, with start and end.

analysis_plan.description: How the result will be computed, including segment cuts decided in advance.

decision_rule.description: The pre-agreed action for each outcome, fixed BEFORE the test runs.

pass.description: Action if the primary metric meets the threshold.

inconclusive.description: Action if the result cannot separate signal from noise - the most commonly omitted and most commonly needed branch.

threshold.description: The numeric threshold separating pass from fail, with units.

status.description: A proposal stays 'proposed' until a human approves it.

result.description: Observed outcome, with its measurement window.

claim_strength.description: 'causal' requires a control, adequate power and a pre-registered rule; otherwise 'directional'.

limitations.description: What the result does not establish.

allOf.description: A running or complete test must state whether its claim is directional or causal.
An empty control cannot support any claim stronger than directional.
